summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored New Zealand documents: 12 versions of the INZ Active Investor Plus statistics page, the 2022 and 2025 INZ announcements, the AIP visa page, a September 2026 ministerial release and five archived Investor 1/2 operational-manual sections. Added every nationality row (applications and people) for each page version, the pre-2025 settings summary on every version, approval-in-principle splits, transitioned vs new applications, potential minimum investment, processing times, withdrawals, the capital-by-investment-type table with its percentage shares, Investor 2 annual caps, and rules (presence days, caps, deadlines, points). Four nationality tables do not add up to their printed totals and one approval-in-principle split does not either; notes say so.

new_indicators.name: Minimum investment of applications received
new_indicators.definition: Sum of the minimum investment amounts of the applications a programme has received in a period (each application counted at its category minimum), as printed by the programme agency, e.g. INZ's 'potential total minimum investment'. Not money invested or committed.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-nzl1 for the INZ Active Investor Plus statistics page (2025-2026 versions). Status projection: it is what the applications would bring if all went ahead. Distinct from rbi_investment_intended (pipeline) and rbi_investment_total (committed).

new_indicators.name: Investment pipeline plus committed capital
new_indicators.definition: One figure printed by the programme agency for investment in the pipeline (applications in progress or approved in principle) plus capital committed by approved investors, cumulative from a start date.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-nzl1 for INZ/ministerial headline totals (e.g. "around NZD $5.15 billion have been added to the investment pipeline or committed"). Sources usually also print the parts, recorded as rbi_investment_intended and rbi_investment_total; this keeps the headline without adding them up.
